title: Network congestion in Melbourne due to a lost network link
current_summary: The issue affecting our network in Melbourne has been resolved. The link that was lost has been restored, and traffic is no longer being rerouted over alternate paths. Customers in Victoria who noticed slower speeds due to congestion should now see normal performance. If you are still experiencing problems, please contact our support team.

cause.reason: A link in our Melbourne ring network was lost, so traffic is using alternate links and causing some congestion.

updates.content: We are aware of an issue affecting our network in Melbourne. We have lost a link in our Melbourne ring network, and traffic is now using alternate links, which has caused some congestion. Some customers in Victoria may notice slower performance. We have moved traffic around the network to ease the congestion. We will share another update as soon as we have more information.

The link in our Melbourne network that was lost has been restored as of 6:38 pm AEDT on 12 October 2026. Traffic has returned to its normal paths and the congestion that was causing slower speeds in Victoria is resolved. This incident is now closed.
